info.title: WS-APIv3 Documentation
info.description:
The Web Services API v3 (WS-APIv3) provides a more flexible and powerful way to perform storage management tasks than the Command Line Interface (CLI). Use WS-APIv3 to automate your management tasks for hosts, ports, volumes, and more.
A developer's guide to the Web Services API v3 is available at https://www.hpe.com/support/AlletraMP-B10000-WSAPIV3-devguide
The OpenAPI specification can be downloaded at OpenAPI Specification (JSON)

API conventions:
  • This document conforms to the OpenAPI 3.1 standard: https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0
  • All requests must include the Content-Type: application/json header.
  • You must authenticate before downloading the OpenAPI document.
  • To authenticate, use POST@/api/v3/credentials with request body {"user": "{{username}}","password": "{{password}}"}
  • Prefer session cookies over bearer tokens for authentication. When using non-password authentication methods, such as MFA, OAuth, or CaC cards, session cookies are mandatory.
  • application sets, appsets, virtual volume set, vvset are all the same thing. These are referred to as "applicationsets" in API endpoints and "APPSET" in schema types
  • The description of a field in the schema will often state the units of the value. Units are sometimes expressed at the end of the field name, e.g. sizeMiB.
  • Each resource schema in components/schemas may include an x-endpoint field that specifies the canonical REST collection endpoint for that resource (e.g., "x-endpoint": "/api/v3/systems"). When looking up which endpoint to query for a given schema type, check the schema's x-endpoint field first.
  • Subaction schemas (used with POST /api/v3/provisioning) include an x-main-action field that names the batch action they belong to (e.g., "x-main-action": "CREATE_COMPLEX_APPSET"). Subactions must be submitted as a list in the operations array of the main batch action body: {"batch": "<x-main-action>", "ordered": true, "operations": [{"action": "<subaction>", "parameters": {...}}, ...]}.
  • When trying to find a field corresponding to a vague description (e.g., "ransomware confidence"):
    1. Do a fuzzy search of the description fields in the schemas to identify the actual field name (e.g., rwareConfidence).
    2. Find which schema contains that field using: jq -r 'paths(type == "object" and has("FIELDNAME")) | join(".")' openapi_wsapiv3_en-US.json
    3. Check if the field is nested (e.g., under .parameters, .properties, etc.) based on the schema path.
    4. Use the correct nested path when querying the API (e.g., .members[].parameters.rwareConfidence not just .members[].rwareConfidence).
    5. The system's timezone can be found in the timeZone field of GET@/server/info. Unless otherwise specified, timestamps are in the timezone of the system.

get.summary: Get audit log entries
get.description:
Retrieve audit log entries from the operating system on demand.
Results are fetched directly per request with no cache.
**Filtering:** All query parameters are optional. Time range can be specified with minMinutes (last N minutes) or startTime/endTime (epoch seconds). String filters (username, role, ipAddr, opName, objectName, result) are case-insensitive substring matches applied after retrieval.
**Use Cases:** Review recent security-relevant operations, audit user activity by role or IP address, investigate specific object modifications.
**Examples:** Retrieve all failed operations in the last hour: `?minMinutes=60&result=Failed`
Retrieve all operations performed by a specific user in a time range: `?startTime=1700000000&endTime=1700086400&username=user`

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description:
This contains the WSAPI session key that was returned by the server after a successful user authentication request.
See [RFC6749](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749) and [RFC6750](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750) for more information.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description:
Acceptable client response formats. Must be one of the following:

- application/json

parameters.name: minMinutes
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Return entries from the last N minutes. Must be a positive integer. Cannot be used together with startTime or endTime.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Start of time range as Unix epoch seconds (inclusive). Must be a non-negative integer. Must be provided together with endTime and must not exceed endTime. Cannot be used together with minMinutes.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Filter entries by user role (case-insensitive substring match).

parameters.name: ipAddr
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Filter entries by client IP address or port (case-insensitive substring match).

parameters.name: maxRecords
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Maximum number of records to return. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 10000. Defaults to 1000.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
End of time range as Unix epoch seconds (inclusive). Must be a non-negative integer. Must be provided together with startTime and must not precede startTime. Cannot be used together with minMinutes.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Filter entries by username (case-insensitive substring match).

parameters.name: opName
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Filter entries by operation name (case-insensitive substring match).

parameters.name: objectName
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Filter entries by the name of the object acted upon (case-insensitive substring match).

parameters.name: result
parameters.description:
Available since v2.6.0
Filter entries by result: Success, Failed, or Requested (case-insensitive substring match).

get.summary: Get event log entries
get.description:
Retrieve event log entries from the operating system on demand.
Results are fetched directly per request with no cache.
**Filtering:** All query parameters are optional. Time range can be specified with minMinutes (last N minutes) or startTime/endTime (epoch seconds). String filters (severity, class, component, type) are case-insensitive substring matches applied after retrieval.
**Use Cases:** Review recent system events, filter events by severity or component, investigate hardware or configuration events.
**Examples:** Retrieve all fatal events in the last hour: `?minMinutes=60&severity=Fatal`
Retrieve all events for a specific time range: `?startTime=1700000000&endTime=1700086400&class=Alert`

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description:

parameters.name: endTime

parameters.name: class
parameters.description:

parameters.name: component

delete.description: Dismissing a volume from a Remote Copy group. Use query parameters to control dismissal behavior. Note: Do not use keepSnap and removeSecondaryVolume at the same time.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description:
This contains the WSAPI session key that was returned by the server after a successful user authentication request.
See [RFC6749](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749) and [RFC6750](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750) for more information.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description:
Acceptable client response formats. Must be one of the following:

- application/json

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the resource

parameters.name: removeSecondaryVolume
parameters.description: If true, removes the secondary virtual volume from the target system and deletes it.

parameters.name: keepAlua
parameters.description: If true, keeps the local volume ALUA state from changing. Used during Peer Motion migrations.

parameters.name: keepRemoteExport
parameters.description: If true, retains the remote volume export on the target system.

parameters.name: keepLocalVVinVVset
parameters.description: If true, keeps the local volume as a member of its virtual volume set after dismissal. If false (default), the local volume is removed from its virtual volume set.

parameters.name: removeLocalVV
parameters.description: If true, deletes the local volume while removing it from the replication group.

parameters.name: peer
parameters.description: If true, allows removal of a peer volume from the group. The peer volume must be part of a Peer Motion Consistency Group.

parameters.name: keepSnap
parameters.description: If true, retains the local volume resynchronization snapshot after dismissal.

get.summary: Used to query all available software updates visible to the user
get.description:
Returns all available software update that are visible to the user.

An available software update represents a recommended or staged OS version that the system may be updated to, and the latest download, readiness, and installation status for that package. This resource updates in real time.

An empty response signifies that there are no available software updates visible to the current user.

A recommended package may be automatically staged without user action. If not, a package should first be staged.

Best practice is to run readiness checks on a package within 7 days of performing a software update.

When an update completes successfully, it is no longer an available package. Successful software updates can be checked in the softwarestatus endpoint.

post.summary: Used to perform an action on an available software update
post.description:
Allows the user to perform one of the following actions on an available software update:

- DOWNLOAD - starts the download and staging of the update package on the system

- READINESS_CHECK - starts the readiness checks for the update package on the system. This should be run before performing an update, and will ensure system is in good state to begin software update. If the package is not downloaded, it will be downloaded before the checks are run.

- UPDATE - starts an update operation for the update package on the system. If the update to this package is stopped with state FAILED or FAILED_WITH_WARN, this call will instead start an update retry operation. If the update is stopped with state COMPLETED_WITH_WARN, this call will instead start an update resume operation.

The update package's status is updated in real time as the operation proceeds.

Returns a single software update status resource corresponding to the given UID, if the user has access to it.

A software update status resource represents the current state of an operation to update the OS version. This resource updates in real time.

post.summary: Used to upload and stage a new software package
post.description:
Using multipart/form-data upload, sends a software package file to the system to be staged. If it is a valid software package, it will be staged and can then have checks and update actions run on it.

There is no json payload for this API call, and just a file upload: using curl utility or similar, a file can be uploaded with a format like 'curl -X POST "api/v3/softwareupdate/upload" -F "file=@/path/to/package"'

File name must be a valid package name, and the file being uploaded must be of file format .star or .iso.

vlanId.description:
validation: omitempty,vlan_id
The VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) identifier for the iSCSI port used in network segmentation.
**Typical Value:** Integer from 1 to 4094, common values like 10, 100, 1000, or 0 for untagged.
**Constraints:** Must be valid VLAN ID in range 0-4094 (0 means untagged, 4095 reserved). Only applicable for iSCSI migrations. Both source and target ports must be on same VLAN for connectivity.
**Usage:** Enables network isolation and traffic segmentation for iSCSI migration data. Must match across peer link endpoints for successful connection.
**Example:** 28 (for tagged VLAN), 0 (for untagged/native VLAN)

RetentionTime.description:
Specifies the amount of time, relative to the current time, that the volume will be retained. Time is a positive integer value and in the range of 1 minute - 1825 days.
Note: If the volume is not in any domain, then its retention time cannot exceed the value of the system's VVRetentionTimeMax. The default value for the system's VVRetentionTimeMax is 14 days. If the volume belongs to a domain, then its retention time cannot exceed the value of the domain's VVRetentionTimeMax, if set. The retention time cannot be removed or reduced once it is set. If the volume has its retention time set, it cannot be removed within its retention time. If both expiration time and retention time are specified, then the retention time cannot be longer than the expiration time.

expireSecs.description: Expiration value specified for volume snapshot

online.description: Specifies that the copy is to be performed online. This means that the  destination can be immediately exported and is automatically created by  this command, meaning that it cannot exist prior to executing this  command. This option requires the specification of a CPG for the  destination volume and allows for the options listed below. Finally,  online is incompatible with enableResync and skipZero. The reduce option is optional; when omitted, a thinly provisioned destination volume is created.

priority.description: Specifies the priority of the copy operation when it is started

reduce.description: Indicates that the volume the online copy creates should be a volume using both the dedup and compression technologies. Without this option a thinly provisioned volume is created

selectionType.title: selectiontype.Enum

skipZero.description: When copying from a thinly provisioned source, only copy allocated portions of the source virtual volume. Using this option can save time, but only use  it if the destination is newly created or has been re-initialized to  zero. If there is pre-existing data in the destination virtual volume, it will not be  overwritten to match the source virtual volume if the same offset is not allocated  in the source. This option cannot be combined with enableResync or online.
